paper_title: MedEthicsQA A Comprehensive Question Answering Benchmark for Medical   Ethics Evaluation of LLMs
caption: Illustration of taxonomy on medical ethics. The inner circle encapsulates four pillar principles in medicine, and the outer circle represents the 26 categories clustered from 256 detailed principles.
model_annotation: The pie chart visually illustrates a taxonomy of medical ethics, structured as a two-tiered circular diagram. The inner circle is divided into four color-coded segments representing the foundational ethical principles in medicine: “Beneficence” (large blue segment), “Non-Maleficence” (purple), “Autonomy” (green), and “Justice” (orange). Surrounding this core, the outer ring is segmented into 26 distinct categories—each corresponding to a cluster of detailed ethical principles derived from a larger set of 256—radiating outward and aligned with their respective pillar. For instance, under “Beneficence,” categories include “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” and “Ethical Research”; under “Non-Maleficence,” we see “Prevent Patient from Harm” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain”; “Autonomy” encompasses “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed” and “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication”; and “Justice” includes “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally” and “Promote Environmental Sustainability.” Each outer segment is labeled with its specific ethical category and is color-matched to its parent principle in the inner circle, creating a clear visual hierarchy that maps granular ethical duties to their overarching moral foundations. The chart serves as a conceptual framework for organizing and evaluating medical ethical reasoning, particularly in the context of benchmarking large language models’ understanding of medical ethics as described in the MedEthicsQA paper.
